lessons.title: WebAssembly Fundamentals
lessons.html:
WebAssembly Crash Course

WebAssembly runs at native speed in browsers. Rust → WASM = unbeatable performance + safety.

Stack vs WASM:

  • JavaScript: Dynamic, GC, interpreted
  • WASM: Static, no GC, compiled to machine code

Development Flow:

1. cargo new --lib wasm-game
2. trunk init (or wasm-pack)
3. cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown
4. wasm-bindgen --out-dir pkg/ target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/debug/wasm_game.wasm
5. trunk serve

Practice Exercises:

  1. Modify the code example to handle edge cases
  2. Write a test case for the main functionality
  3. Refactor the code to improve performance or readability

Key Takeaways:

  • Understanding the fundamental concepts is crucial for advanced topics
  • Always consider edge cases and error handling in production code
  • Practice with real-world examples to solidify your knowledge

WASM-Specific Optimizations

Make your WASM blazing fast with these techniques.

Memory Management:

#[wasm_bindgen]
pub fn process_array(input: &[f32]) -> Vec<f32> {
    let mut output: Vec<f32> = vec![0.0; input.len()];
    
    input.iter().enumerate().for_each(|(i, &val)| {
        output[i] = val * 2.5; // SIMD friendly
    });
    
    output
}

use yew::prelude::*;

#[function_component(Counter)]
fn counter() -> Html {
    let count = use_state(|| 0);
    
    let onclick = {
        let count = count.clone();
        move |_| set_count(*count + 1)
    };
    
    html! {
        <div>
            <button {onclick}>{"+1"}</button>
            <p>{"Count: "}{(*count).to_string()}{""}</p>
        </div>
    }

lessons.title: Web Workers & Multithreading
lessons.html:
Multithreading in the Browser

Web Workers run JavaScript in background threads. Rust compiled to WASM can offload heavy computation.

Worker Setup:

// worker.js
import * as wasm from './pkg/wasm_game.js';

self.onmessage = async (e) => {
    await wasm.default();
    const result = wasm.heavy_computation(e.data);
    self.postMessage(result);
};

// main.js
const worker = new Worker('worker.js', { type: 'module' });
worker.postMessage({ iterations: 1000000 });
worker.onmessage = (e) => {
    console.log('Result from worker:', e.data);
};

Shared Memory (Atomics):

use wasm_bindgen::prelude::*;
use js_sys::SharedArrayBuffer;
use js_sys::Int32Array;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicI32, Ordering};

#[wasm_bindgen]
pub fn increment_in_shared_buffer(buffer: &SharedArrayBuffer) {
    let array = Int32Array::new(buffer);
    // Atomically increment first element
    let ptr = array.as_ptr() as *mut AtomicI32;
    unsafe {
        (*ptr).fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
    }
}

Practice Exercises:

  1. Offload image processing to a web worker
  2. Use SharedArrayBuffer for shared state
  3. Benchmark single-threaded vs multi-threaded WASM

Key Takeaways:

  • Workers run in separate threads
  • SharedArrayBuffer enables shared memory
  • Atomics ensure safe concurrent access

lessons.title: WASM Audio Processing
lessons.html:
Real-Time Audio with Rust

WASM enables low-latency audio processing in the browser. Perfect for synthesizers and effects.

Audio Generator:

use wasm_bindgen::prelude::*;

#[wasm_bindgen]
pub struct AudioGenerator {
    phase: f64,
    sample_rate: f64,
}

#[wasm_bindgen]
impl AudioGenerator {
    pub fn new(sample_rate: f64) -> Self {
        AudioGenerator { phase: 0.0, sample_rate }
    }

    pub fn generate_sine(&mut self, frequency: f64, amplitude: f64, buffer: &mut [f32]) {
        let increment = frequency / self.sample_rate;
        for sample in buffer.iter_mut() {
            *sample = (self.phase * std::f64::consts::TAU).sin() as f32 * amplitude as f32;
            self.phase = (self.phase + increment) % 1.0;
        }
    }

    pub fn generate_sawtooth(&mut self, frequency: f64, amplitude: f64, buffer: &mut [f32]) {
        let increment = frequency / self.sample_rate;
        for sample in buffer.iter_mut() {
            *sample = (self.phase * 2.0 - 1.0) as f32 * amplitude as f32;
            self.phase = (self.phase + increment) % 1.0;
        }
    }
}

JavaScript Integration:

const AudioContext = window.AudioContext || window.webkitAudioContext;
const ctx = new AudioContext();
const gen = AudioGenerator.new(ctx.sampleRate);

// Create ScriptProcessor for real-time audio
const processor = ctx.createScriptProcessor(4096, 0, 1);
processor.onaudioprocess = (event) => {
    const output = event.outputBuffer.getChannelData(0);
    gen.generate_sine(440.0, 0.3, output);  // 440Hz sine wave
};

processor.connect(ctx.destination);

  2. Add low-pass and high-pass filters
  3. Implement a drum machine with sample triggers

Key Takeaways:

  • WASM audio has minimal latency
  • Processing runs at native speed
  • ScriptProcessorNode bridges JS and WASM

lessons.title: WASM Game Development
lessons.html:
Building Games with Rust + WASM

Rust + WASM provides 60fps game performance with memory safety. Combine with Canvas API for graphics.

Game Loop:

use wasm_bindgen::prelude::*;
use web_sys::CanvasRenderingContext2d;

#[wasm_bindgen]
pub struct Game {
    ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2d,
    player_x: f64,
    player_y: f64,
    score: u32,
    enemies: Vec<Enemy>,
}

#[wasm_bindgen]
impl Game {
    pub fn new(canvas_id: &str) -> Result<Game, JsValue> {
        let document = web_sys::window().unwrap().document().unwrap();
        let canvas = document.get_element_by_id(canvas_id).unwrap();
        let canvas: web_sys::HtmlCanvasElement = canvas.dyn_into()?;
        let ctx = canvas.get_context("2d")?.unwrap().dyn_into()?;

        Ok(Game {
            ctx,
            player_x: 400.0,
            player_y: 300.0,
            score: 0,
            enemies: Vec::new(),
        })
    }

    pub fn update(&mut self) {
        // Move enemies
        for enemy in &mut self.enemies {
            enemy.x -= enemy.speed;
        }
        // Remove off-screen enemies
        self.enemies.retain(|e| e.x > -50.0);
        // Check collisions
        self.check_collisions();
        // Spawn new enemies
        if js_sys::Math::random() < 0.02 {
            self.enemies.push(Enemy::new());
        }
    }

    pub fn render(&self) {
        self.ctx.clear_rect(0.0, 0.0, 800.0, 600.0);

        // Draw player
        self.ctx.set_fill_style(&JsValue::from_str("blue"));
        self.ctx.fill_rect(self.player_x, self.player_y, 50.0, 50.0);

        // Draw enemies
        self.ctx.set_fill_style(&JsValue::from_str("red"));
        for enemy in &self.enemies {
            self.ctx.fill_rect(enemy.x, enemy.y, 30.0, 30.0);
        }

        // Draw score
        self.ctx.set_fill_style(&JsValue::from_str("black"));
        self.ctx.set_font(&JsValue::from_str("24px Arial"));
        self.ctx.fill_text(&JsValue::from_str(&format!("Score: {}", self.score)), 10.0, 30.0).unwrap();
    }
}

Practice Exercises:

  1. Create a space shooter game with keyboard input
  2. Add particle effects for explosions
  3. Implement a level system with increasing difficulty

Key Takeaways:

  • canvas provides hardware-accelerated 2D rendering
  • Game loop pattern: update state, then render
  • Rust ownership prevents data races in game state

lessons.title: WASM with WebGL
lessons.html:
3D Graphics with Rust and WebGL

WebGL provides GPU-accelerated 3D graphics. Rust can compile shaders and manage GPU buffers efficiently.

WebGL Setup:

use wasm_bindgen::prelude::*;
use web_sys::{WebGlRenderingContext, WebGlProgram, WebGlShader};

fn compile_shader(
    ctx: &WebGlRenderingContext,
    shader_type: u32,
    source: &str,
) -> Result<WebGlShader, String> {
    let shader = ctx.create_shader(shader_type).ok_or("Unable to create shader")?;
    ctx.shader_source(&shader, source);
    ctx.compile_shader(&shader);

    if ctx.get_shader_parameter(&shader, WebGlRenderingContext::COMPILE_STATUS).as_bool().unwrap_or(false) {
        Ok(shader)
    } else {
        Err(ctx.get_shader_info_log(&shader).unwrap_or_else(|| String::from("Unknown error")))
    }
}

#[wasm_bindgen]
pub fn init_webgl(canvas_id: &str) -> Result<(), JsValue> {
    let document = web_sys::window().unwrap().document().unwrap();
    let canvas = document.get_element_by_id(canvas_id).unwrap();
    let canvas: web_sys::HtmlCanvasElement = canvas.dyn_into()?;
    let ctx: WebGlRenderingContext = canvas.get_context("webgl")?.unwrap().dyn_into()?;

    // Vertex shader
    let vs_source = r#"
        attribute vec2 position;
        uniform vec2 u_resolution;

        void main() {
            vec2 clip_space = position / u_resolution * 2.0 - 1.0;
            gl_Position = vec4(clip_space, 0.0, 1.0);
        }
    "#;

    // Fragment shader
    let fs_source = r#"
        precision mediump float;
        uniform vec4 u_color;

        void main() {
            gl_FragColor = u_color;
        }
    "#;

    let vs = compile_shader(&ctx, WebGlRenderingContext::VERTEX_SHADER, vs_source)?;
    let fs = compile_shader(&ctx, WebGlRenderingContext::FRAGMENT_SHADER, fs_source)?;
    let program = ctx.create_program().ok_or("Unable to create program")?;

    ctx.attach_shader(&program, &vs);
    ctx.attach_shader(&program, &fs);
    ctx.link_program(&program);

    ctx.use_program(Some(&program));

    // Clear to blue
    ctx.clear_color(0.0, 0.0, 0.5, 1.0);
    ctx.clear(WebGlRenderingContext::COLOR_BUFFER_BIT);

    Ok(())
}

Practice Exercises:

  1. Draw a rotating 3D cube with perspective
  2. Add matrix transformations for camera movement
  3. Implement a simple 3D scene with multiple objects

Key Takeaways:

  • WebGL allows GPU computation from WASM
  • Shaders run on the GPU for parallel rendering
  • Buffers transfer vertex data to the GPU

lessons.title: WASM Optimization & Profiling
lessons.html:
Performance Tuning for WASM

Optimizing WASM binary size and runtime performance is crucial for web deployment.

Binary Size Optimization:

// Cargo.toml optimizations
[profile.release]
lto = true
opt-level = "z"   # Optimize for size
codegen-units = 1
strip = true
panic = "abort"   # No panic unwinding

// .cargo/config.toml
[target.wasm32-unknown-unknown]
rustflags = ["-C", "target-feature=+bulk-memory"]

// Use twiggy to analyze WASM binary
// cargo install twiggy
// twiggy top pkg/wasm_game_bg.wasm

Runtime Optimization:

// Avoid unnecessary allocations
// BAD: Creating Strings repeatedly
fn process(data: &[f32]) -> Vec<f32> {
    data.iter().map(|x| x * 2.0).collect()
}

// GOOD: Use pre-allocated buffer
#[wasm_bindgen]
pub fn process_in_place(data: &mut [f32]) {
    for x in data.iter_mut() {
        *x *= 2.0;
    }
}

// Use typed arrays for JS interop
#[wasm_bindgen]
pub fn sum_f32_array(arr: &[f32]) -> f32 {
    arr.iter().sum()
}

Practice Exercises:

  1. Profile WASM with browser DevTools
  2. Reduce binary size by 50% with optimization flags
  3. Benchmark typed arrays vs JS arrays for data transfer

Key Takeaways:

  • opt-level = "z" minimizes binary size
  • Pre-allocated buffers avoid GC pressure
  • Typed arrays are zero-copy between JS and WASM
